teams.heading: England Women Crush Australia With Resurgent Seven-Try Second-Half Performance Display
teams.body: England launched their WXV Global Series campaign with a resounding 48-15 victory over Australia in Salford. Despite trailing 10-5 at half-time—a rarity for the side—John Mitchell’s squad produced a clinical second-half display, crossing for seven tries to extend their winning streak to 39 matches. Mitchell dismissed early concerns, noting, "It is an absolute joke if you are worried about being down 10-5," instead praising the group’s ability to solve problems after a competitive opening period of pre-season rugby.

teams.heading: IRFU Confirms There Are No Plans For Six Nations US Games
teams.body: The IRFU has officially dismissed suggestions that Ireland could play a Six Nations fixture in the United States. Following comments from World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin regarding the potential for matches to be hosted stateside to drive growth, the union clarified that there are "currently no plans or discussions" regarding such a move. The IRFU stated that the competition holds a unique place for supporters, and the chance to play at home remains central to the tournament's enduring appeal.

lead.why: The IRFU's definitive statement regarding the speculation over moving Six Nations fixtures to the US settles a major talking point.

teams.body: Scotland suffered a heavy 64-26 defeat to Canada in their WXV Series opener at Hive Stadium. Despite tries from Evie Gallagher, Shona Campbell, Lana Skeldon, and Rhona Lloyd, the visitors’ attacking pace proved too difficult to contain as Canada crossed for 10 tries. Interim head coach Dave Butcher faces a significant challenge to bolster the team's defensive physicality ahead of the upcoming fixtures against New Zealand and Australia, as the squad looks to move past a difficult start to the tournament.
